NOVEMBER 20, 2026 -  DLA is providing formal responses to a  selection of critical industry questions  received in response to the RFI for the Whole-of-Government (WoG) ordering platform (WBOS). These specific questions are being answered in advance to assist industry in their strategic preparations for the upcoming virtual Industry Day. Responses to additional pending inquiries will be integrated into the Industry Day briefing on December 2 or addressed via a separate, forthcoming pre-solicitation update. 

  ATTACHMENT WITH RESPONSES IS INCLUDED BELOW.  

 ************************************************************************* 

  DEFENSE LOGISTICS AGENCY (DLA) TROOP SUPPORT  

  CLOTHING AND TEXTILES DIRECTORATE — PHILADELPHIA, PA  

  REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) & SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE  

  Whole-of-Government Web-Based Ordering System (WBOS) & Commercial eMarketplace Platform  

  FEDERAL MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE (FAR 15.201(e) & FAR Part 10): This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for market research, planning, and information-gathering purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO), or an obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services. The Government is seeking broad industry input on commercial capabilities, architectural options, and market readiness. Responses are strictly voluntary; the Government will not reimburse any costs associated with preparing or submitting responses to this notice.  

  1. Executive Summary & Purpose of Inquiry  

 The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Troop Support Clothing and Textiles (C&T) Directorate is conducting market research to explore commercial software solutions, digital eMarketplace architectures, and industry best practices for deploying a next-generation Web-Based Ordering System (WBOS). DLA’s Troop Support C&T organization serves as the Federal Government’s primary enterprise manager for military clothing and textiles, working extensively with domestic industry. DLA is currently assessing the expansion of this shared-services procurement model to serve civilian Whole-of-Government (WOG) partner agencies, including the Department of the Interior (DOI), Department of Justice (DOJ), Department of Transportation (DOT), Department of State (DOS), and Department of Homeland Security (DHS). 

 The primary objective of this RFI is to engage commercial e-commerce developers, SaaS providers, systems integrators, and domestic textile industry stakeholders. DLA seeks to understand what commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) and Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) capabilities exist today, how commercial technology can resolve complex federal supply chain and fiscal integration challenges, and what industry recommendations DLA should incorporate into its upcoming acquisition strategy. DLA is committed to adopting commercial best practices and avoiding custom development wherever commercial platforms can satisfy or be adapted to meet mission requirements.

  3. Mission Needs & Strategic Challenges  

 The contemplated capability would enable Government-approved vendors to list and maintain Government-approved catalogs; enable authorized agency personnel to purchase authorized items; apply agency-specific eligibility, entitlement/allowance, item-authorization, approval, and management-control rules; support authorized payment methods; and provide auditable transaction, fulfillment, and program-management information. 

 To modernize uniform procurement across DoD and civilian partner agencies, any future solution must address several interrelated operational and regulatory challenges. Rather than dictating prescriptive technical designs, DLA outlines the desired functional outcomes below to invite innovative, industry-driven solutions: 

  Operational Domain: The Operational Challenge / Desired Outcome  

 Commercial Marketplace & User Experience: Deliver a modern, consumer-grade multi-tenant e-commerce experience with sub-second catalog search, faceted filtering, mobile responsiveness, and intuitive uniform selection, while supporting distinct tenant agency branding (DoD, DOI, DOJ, DOT, DOS, DHS) and role-based permissions.
